title: Station Master and Railway NTPC Careers
summary: Guide to Railway Non-Technical Popular Categories (NTPC) exams for Station Master & more.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction

The Railway NTPC Careers offers candidates an incredible opportunity for a secure and prestigious career. It requires candidates to clear a multi-tier selection process that rigorously tests their aptitude, physical fitness, and overall capability. Thousands of aspirants apply every year, making it one of the most competitive career paths available today. Strategic preparation based on the latest examination syllabus is vital to stand out and succeed.

## Eligibility Criteria

| Parameter | Requirements |
|---|---|
| **Educational Qualification** | 12th Pass or Graduate Degree depending on the post applied for (Undergraduate or Graduate posts). |
| **Nationality** | Must be a citizen of India, a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated with the intention of permanently settling. |
| **Stream/Subject** | Any stream is applicable. |
| **Minimum Percentage** | Usually 50% for unreserved categories for undergraduate posts. |
| **Document Verification** | Valid ID proof, educational certificates, domicile, and category certificates must be produced in original at the final stages. |
| **Additional Diplomas** | Typing proficiency is required for Junior Clerk / Typist positions. |
| **Computer Literacy** | Mandatory. Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) required for Station Master. |

## Age Limit & Relaxation

| Category | Base Age Limit | Age Relaxation Years |
|---|---|---|
| **General (UR)** | 18 - 30 (UG), 18 - 33 (Grad) | None (0 Years) |
| **Other Backward Classes (OBC)** | 18 - 30 (UG), 18 - 33 (Grad) | Up to 3 Years upper age relaxation |
| **Scheduled Castes (SC)** | 18 - 30 (UG), 18 - 33 (Grad) | Up to 5 Years upper age relaxation |
| **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** | 18 - 30 (UG), 18 - 33 (Grad) | Up to 5 Years upper age relaxation |
| **Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)** | Applicable | Up to 10 Years upper age relaxation (General), 13 (OBC), 15 (SC/ST) |
| **Ex-Servicemen (ESM)** | As per standard guidelines | Typically 3 years after deduction of military service rendered |
| **Departmental Candidates** | As per standard guidelines | Up to 40/45 years of age based on years of continuous service |

## Physical Standards & Test

| Parameter | Male Standard | Female Standard |
|---|---|---|
| **Minimum Height** | As per medical standards | As per medical standards |
| **Chest (Unexpanded)** | Not Applicable | Not Applicable |
| **Chest Expansion** | Not Applicable | Not Applicable |
| **Weight** | Proportionate to height and age as per medical standards | Proportionate to height and age as per medical standards |
| **Running (Sprint)** | N/A | N/A |
| **Long Jump** | N/A | N/A |
| **High Jump** | N/A | N/A |
| **Vision / Eye Sight** | Minimum 6/9, 6/9 without glasses for Station Master (A-2 standard). Highly strict visual parameters. | Minimum 6/9, 6/9 without glasses for Station Master (A-2 standard). Highly strict visual parameters. |

## Written Exam Pattern

| Subject / Section | Total Questions | Maximum Marks | Duration / Time Allowed | Negative Marking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **General Awareness** | 40 Questions (CBT-1) | 40 Marks | Combined with other sections | 1/3 per incorrect answer |
| **Mathematics** | 30 Questions (CBT-1) | 30 Marks | Combined with other sections | 1/3 per incorrect answer |
| **General Intelligence and Reasoning** | 30 Questions (CBT-1) | 30 Marks | Combined with other sections | 1/3 per incorrect answer |
| **Overall Grand Total (CBT-1)** | **100 Questions**| **100 Marks**| **90 Minutes** | **Applicable uniformly** |

## Preparation Strategy Overview

| Preparation Phase | Recommended Action Plan for Candidates |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1: Foundation Building** | Understand the complete syllabus thoroughly. Collect standard reference books, study materials, and begin clearing fundamental concepts across all subjects. |
| **Phase 2: Intensive Practice** | Solve previous year question papers. Enroll in structured mock test series. Analyze performance metrics, identify weak areas, and allocate extra time to improve them. |
| **Phase 3: Final Revision** | Create short, crisp notes for quick recall. Focus on current affairs of the last six months. Avoid picking up completely new topics just before the exam. |
| **Phase 4: Physical & Mental Health**| Maintain a balanced diet, ensure adequate sleep, and incorporate daily physical exercises to clear medical and physical efficiency tests effortlessly. |

We emphasize to all candidates that the details provided above are intended to give you a clear, structured overview of the recruitment framework. Please note that specific numbers, dates, and requirements are subject to modifications as determined by the official recruiting authority. It is highly advised to continually reference the official notification for the most accurate, binding, and up-to-date parameters. Candidates should align their preparation strategies rigorously with the official guidelines to ensure maximum compliance and readiness for all stages.
